observations: Photo 0 shows a car engine bay/engine assembly laid out on the ground/bench area, with many hoses, wiring, and metal components visible.
No full vehicle body, VIN plate, dashboard, or exterior Lexus/LX badges are visible.
The engine appears partially disassembled/removed (not installed in a vehicle).
No clear readable engine model/serial number is visible in the photo.

claims.evidence: Photo 0 does not show a readable Lexus/LX460 identification, VIN/engine code, or any Japan-origin documentation.

risks.risk: Engine may not be LX460 (wrong engine code/model) even if it looks similar; seller text can be incorrect.
risks.proof: A clear close-up photo of the engine code/label (engine block stamping/ID plate) and the transmission bellhousing code if applicable.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as an unknown used engine (worst case: not confirmed to be LX460 and not confirmed working).

risks.risk: Unknown working condition (may be seized, missing parts, or have internal damage).
risks.proof: Video of a cold start (or at minimum a compression test/leak-down test results) plus a short clip showing it running smoothly.

risks.risk: Missing components or incomplete assembly (common with removed engines).
risks.proof: Photo checklist: intake manifold, alternator, starter, sensors, ECU, wiring harness connectors, turbo (if any), and all accessories laid out and counted.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as incomplete/parts may be missing.

risks.risk: Damage from shipping/handling or prior overheating (cracks, bent brackets, burnt wiring).
risks.proof: High-resolution photos of critical areas: cylinder head surface, coolant passages, wiring harness condition, and any visible cracks/burn marks.

risks.risk: ECU/immobilizer mismatch risk (even if engine is correct, electronics may not pair).
risks.proof: Photos of ECU part number label and any immobilizer-related modules; confirm what exactly is included.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as requiring additional electronics/compatibility work.

proof_requests: Clear close-up of the engine code/ID plate stamped on the engine block (and any transmission code if included).
Video proof of start/run (or compression/leak-down test results).
Photos showing what is included in the package (ECU, harness, alternator, starter, sensors, manifolds) laid out and counted.
Photos of any visible damage: cracks, burnt wiring, coolant/oil leaks, and head/cylinder surfaces.
response.reason: From photo 0, the item is an engine assembly but the LX460 identity and working condition cannot be verified remotely; pricing without engine code and proof of operation would be too risky.
